reports.title: Dawn Gill
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The Trust is moving in 2019-20 to electronic prescribing. This will eliminate the need for paper based drug charts, and the attendant risk of them being mislaid or lost.
promises.summary: Implement electronic prescribing system to replace paper drug charts

concerns.quote: Ms Gill was a long term drug user and, based on her history, was likely to take illicit drugs whether she was in or out of hospital
concerns.hazard: risk of illicit drug use while inpatient

concerns.quote: Ms Gill was prescribed methadone in hospital and died of a methadone overdose, but her drug chart was not available at inquest and appears to have been lost

Ms [name redacted] room was described as having been searched on numerous occasions overnight, by more than one person, the first time approximately half an hour after she had last been seen, yet her presence under clothing on the floor was not detected until 10am the following day
concerns.hazard: failure to detect patient on floor

concerns.quote: Ms Gill was thought to have left the ward for a cigarette some time before 12.30am, though she was not actually seen leaving. She was wearing her night things. When her absence was discovered, hospital security personnel were not alerted
concerns.hazard: delayed security response to missing patient

reports.title: Vijaykumar Gadhavi: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths
Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Datix reports were generated for the multiple self-harming incidents in July and August 2020. There was no evidence at the inquest, that action and learning had been put in place as a result of these incidents.
concerns.hazard: lack of action on self-harm incidents

concerns.quote: Despite the multiple risk incidents and foreseeability of future hospital admissions, there was no alert or flag placed on Mr [name redacted] records to alert new staff to the complexities and risk in his presentation.
concerns.hazard: missing risk alert on patient records

concerns.quote: Despite awareness of the previous overdoses on the ward, there was no itemised property list, including a list of medications.
The recommendations by the learning disability nurse were not fully put into practice. In particular, there was insufficient involvement of his family.

There were multiple breaches of the Enhanced Care Policy. There was no risk assessment by the allocated nurse; no consideration of the need to break up the shift of the 1:1 carer and no hourly observations kept by the 1:1 carer.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in documenting patients' medication information, which can lead to unsafe prescribing and overdose risks. The earlier case concerned a lost paper drug chart; the later case notes the absence of an itemised property list of medications.
